run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T00:40:32Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by checkout-path failures that began at ~00:40Z and grew to dominate the checkout route. frontend-proxy's own 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' spans began carrying HTTP 500 (10-minute error-span increase for ingress 0 at 00:18:32Z, 8.42 at 00:40:32Z, 44.21 at 00:42:32Z, 296.84 at 00:52:32Z; router frontend egress 0 through 00:40:32Z then 36.84 at 00:42:32Z and 292.63 at 00:50:32Z), while frontend's non-checkout operations stayed at 0 errors. The 500s originate in checkout: checkout's own 'HTTP POST' and 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' spans fail with rpc.grpc.status_code 13 and status description 'shipping quote failure: failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 500'. The deepest failing hop visible in the traces is shipping: its '/get-quote' server span returns 'Internal Server Error' and its 'POST quote' client span (QUOTE_ADDR=http://quote:8080) ends in 'Timeout' after ~5.00s, with no quote-service span in that trace. quote itself was not failing: its own spans are 199-331 us without error status and it keeps logging 'Calculated quote'. The network-level fault is declared only in events: a chaos-mesh Schedule 'otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition' in namespace chaos-mesh spawned a NetworkChaos object every minute from 00:40:26Z, each reporting 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/quote-6b5877698d-8fn9w' and 'otel-demo/shipping-75d58f5d84-jgxvv' and recovering at :21 past each minute, matching the per-minute request/serve bursts in shipping and quote logs. All otel-demo pods were Running/Ready with 0 restarts and the Services for quote, shipping, email, checkout and frontend-proxy had populated endpoints. The conclusion is partial because the fault is evidenced only by events (the Schedule/NetworkChaos specs are not readable here) and the Schedule name mentions an email/checkout partition while only the quote and shipping pods are shown receiving chaos.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own error spans deviated from a near-zero baseline in the incident window: the 10-minute increase of traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",span_name="ingress",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} was 0 at 00:18:32Z and 8.42 at 00:40:32Z, then 44.21 at 00:42:32Z, 295.79 at 00:50:32Z and 296.84 at 00:52:32Z; the 'router frontend egress' error series was 0 through 00:40:32Z and 36.84 at 00:42:32Z and 292.63 at 00:50:32Z.

Before the deviation the checkout path was clean: an instant query at 00:35:00Z (range 00:15:00Z-00:35:00Z) returned 0 error-span increase for frontend 'POST', 'POST /api/checkout', 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' and 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' and for frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress', while frontend-proxy 'ingress' already had a background increase of 14.35 per 20 minutes.

frontend's errors are confined to the checkout route: the 10-minute error-span increase was 35.79 at 00:42:32Z and 290.53 at 00:50:32Z for 'POST /api/checkout', 'POST', 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' and 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder', while 'GET', 'GET /api/cart', 'GET /api/data', 'POST /api/cart', 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart', 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem', 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' and 'tcp.connect' stayed at 0 for the whole window.

checkout itself records the failures: the 10-minute error-span increase for checkout 'HTTP POST' and 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' was 33.00 at 00:42:32Z, 290.53 at 00:50:32Z and 292.63 at 00:52:32Z, all STATUS_CODE_ERROR, starting from zero earlier in the window.

A failing trace (trace_id cfdf4d5ad0a694a5b21b34e15dc11411, 20 spans, none omitted) shows the error chain: load-generator POST -> frontend-proxy 'ingress' (http.status_code 500) -> frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' (500) -> frontend 'POST /api/checkout' (500) -> frontend client 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' (rpc.grpc.status_code 13) -> checkout 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' with otel.status_description 'shipping quote failure: failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 500' -> checkout 'prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart' -> checkout client 'HTTP POST' -> shipping '/get-quote' (otel.status_description 'Internal Server Error') -> shipping client 'POST quote' (otel.status_description 'Timeout', duration 5,000,995 us). The same trace contains no quote-service span.

shipping's failures are its quote call: sampled error traces dated 00:51:49Z-00:51:59Z show shipping '/get-quote' error spans (5,000,518-5,001,391 us) each parented by a checkout 'HTTP POST' span and each parenting a shipping 'POST quote' error span (5,000,448-5,001,336 us) whose status description is 'Timeout'.
shipping's deployment sets QUOTE_ADDR=http://quote:8080 (and no EMAIL_ADDR), so its 'POST quote' client span targets the quote service.

quote was not failing on its own: the 10-minute increase of quote spans ('POST /getquote', 'calculate-quote', '{closure}') fell from 352.63 at 00:40:32Z to 32.50 at 00:56:32Z with status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET and no error series, and a sampled slice of quote traces at 00:50:18Z-00:50:21Z shows 'POST /getquote' server spans of 199-331 us with successful child 'calculate-quote' spans of 24-40 us.

shipping's application log shows requests entering and not completing in bursts: between 00:41:22Z and 00:42:20Z it repeatedly logs 'Requesting quote' without the matching 'Sending Quote'/'Tracking ID Created' lines (for example at 00:41:28.455Z, 00:41:29.809Z, 00:41:36.187Z, 00:42:07.250Z, 00:42:20.538Z), and then logs a burst of 'Sending Quote'/'Tracking ID Created' at 00:42:21.179Z-00:42:24.988Z. quote logs 'Calculated quote' in matching bursts at 00:46:21Z, 00:47:21Z-00:47:26Z, 00:48:21Z-00:48:22Z, 00:49:21Z-00:49:22Z and 00:50:21Z.

Events name a chaos-mesh Schedule 'otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition' (namespace chaos-mesh) that spawned a new NetworkChaos object every minute at 00:40:26Z, 00:41:26Z, 00:42:26Z, 00:43:26Z, 00:44:26Z, 00:45:26Z, 00:46:26Z, 00:47:26Z, 00:48:26Z and 00:49:26Z ('Create new object: otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition-<suffix>', reason Spawned); each child's Started event is followed by 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/quote-6b5877698d-8fn9w' and 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/shipping-75d58f5d84-jgxvv', and a 'Time up according to the duration' plus 'Successfully recover chaos for ...' at :21 past the next minute (for example Started 00:40:26Z, recovered 00:41:21Z).

The event set for the window groups around those chaos objects: NetworkChaos Applied 20, Recovered 18, Started 10, TimeUp 9, Updated 95 in namespace chaos-mesh, and PodNetworkChaos Updated 38 in namespace otel-demo, with the PodNetworkChaos objects named quote-6b5877698d-8fn9w and shipping-75d58f5d84-jgxvv.

All 21 otel-demo pods, including frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-wvxht, checkout-5dccddf8bb-pd7qk, shipping-75d58f5d84-jgxvv, quote-6b5877698d-8fn9w and email-59f69bc6cf-8z5c5, were phase Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and start times 2026-11-18T00:03Z-00:05Z; no container termination reasons or restarts were observed.

The Service endpoints for quote, shipping, email, checkout and frontend-proxy each have one ready address pointing at the expected pod (quote 100.96.1.165 -> quote-6b5877698d-8fn9w, shipping 100.96.1.109 -> shipping-75d58f5d84-jgxvv, email 100.96.2.193 -> email-59f69bc6cf-8z5c5, checkout 100.96.3.186 -> checkout-5dccddf8bb-pd7qk, frontend-proxy 100.96.1.213 -> frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-wvxht).

The network fault injected on the quote and shipping pods (chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition via its per-minute NetworkChaos children) blocks shipping's HTTP call to quote: shipping's 'POST quote' client span times out at ~5s with no quote server span in the trace, quote keeps serving fast whenever a request does arrive, and both shipping and quote show request/serve bursts exactly at :21 past each minute when the chaos experiment recovers. That makes shipping return 500 to checkout, checkout return gRPC 13, frontend return HTTP 500, and frontend-proxy record the 5xx errors the alert measures.

Rejected: the quote service itself is erroring or slow. quote has no error-status span series in the window, its 'POST /getquote' server spans measured 199-331 us with successful 'calculate-quote' children, and quote logged 'Calculated quote' throughout; the requests that fail never produce a quote span.

Rejected: the email service returned the 500 named in the error text. email has no error-status span series in the window (only 'POST /send_order_confirmation', 'send_email' and 'sinatra.render_template' with STATUS_CODE_UNSET), its call volume merely fell from 354.74 per 10 minutes at 00:40:32Z to 38.58 at 00:55:32Z because checkouts now fail before the confirmation step, and the failing trace contains no email span.

Rejected: a node-level network failure on node i-0b4b26fa385533a10 (where quote, shipping and frontend-proxy all run) caused the errors. frontend-proxy on the same node kept serving its normal non-checkout traffic (ingress STATUS_CODE_UNSET volume stayed ~6,000 per 10 minutes and only the checkout path errored), and pods on that node such as product-catalog returned successful sub-100 us spans inside the failing traces.

Rejected: the concurrent data-recorders workload activity explains the frontend-proxy errors. Those events are Deployment ScalingReplicaSet and Job/PVC/StatefulSet activity in namespace data-recorders, unrelated to otel-demo, and the otel-demo error signals are confined to the checkout -> shipping -> quote path; no evidence ties the two.

Other candidate dependencies were checked in the failing window and showed no error spans: cart (successful 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' and 'HGET' spans), currency (successful 'Currency/Convert' with rpc.grpc.status_code 0 and otel.status_code OK) and product-catalog (successful 'oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' spans of 46-67 us) all served correctly inside the failing checkout traces.

Read the chaos-mesh Schedule 'otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition' and its NetworkChaos children directly (kubectl -n chaos-mesh get schedule.networkchaos.chaos-mesh.org / networkchaos) to confirm action, direction, duration, selector and target, and to reconcile why the applied pods are otel-demo/quote-6b5877698d-8fn9w and otel-demo/shipping-75d58f5d84-jgxvv although the name references an email/checkout partition; also confirm whether the experiment is still active beyond 00:49:54Z.

If the injection is not intended, delete or disable the Schedule in namespace chaos-mesh rather than touching shipping, checkout or frontend-proxy, whose pods are healthy (Running, Ready, 0 restarts) and whose endpoints are populated; afterwards verify that the frontend-proxy 'ingress'/'router frontend egress' error increase and the shipping 'POST quote' timeouts return to the pre-00:40Z zero baseline.

Reconcile the error wording 'failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 500' with the shipping->quote call in the shipping/checkout source or image 2.1.3, since shipping has only QUOTE_ADDR set and the failing client span is 'POST quote'; this misleading message is what propagates into the checkout and frontend status descriptions.

gaps: The chaos-mesh Schedule 'otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition' and its NetworkChaos children could not be read as objects (schedule/networkchaos kinds are not available here), so the injected action, direction, mode, durations, selector/target and their current desired phase are unknown; only their events were observed.

The Schedule name references an email/checkout network partition, but the only pods shown receiving chaos are otel-demo/quote-6b5877698d-8fn9w and otel-demo/shipping-75d58f5d84-jgxvv; which selector/target mapping produced that, and whether email or checkout pods were meant to be included, is unresolved.

No alerting rule named RequestErrorRate and no rule group of that name was returned (both queries returned no_data), so the alert's exact expression, the meaning of its 0.6444444444444444 value, and whether it evaluates traces or http_server_request_duration_seconds_count are unknown.

Chaos events are only visible from 00:23:34Z (source_start_at of the event query) and only up to 00:49:54Z, so earlier and later experiment instances are unknown; the error metric still shows failures at the last sampled point 00:56:32Z.

The error text names an 'email service' while the observed failing call is shipping -> 'POST quote'; the shipping source/image could not be inspected to explain the wording, and a query for error/fail/500 lines in the email container from 00:38Z to 00:57Z returned no_data, so email is verified only through span metrics (no error series).
A cluster-wide query for networking.k8s.io networkpolicies returned no_data, so a NetworkPolicy-based explanation could be neither confirmed nor excluded.
A checkout pod log query for 'shipping quote|error|fail' over 00:40:00Z-00:57:00Z returned no_data while spans clearly record the failures, so checkout's error logging is incompletely characterized.
Change history is not integrated, so who created or last modified the chaos Schedule, and when, cannot be verified.

The alert fired at 00:40:32Z while the first chaos experiment in the visible events started at 00:40:26Z and the first ~5s shipping timeouts follow seconds later; the exact request that tripped the threshold and the alert's evaluation window are unverified.

Several views behind these findings were incomplete or truncated: the shipping-error trace search was capped at the 5 traces requested (incomplete), the shipping and quote log reads were newest-N capped (incomplete), and the quote trace slice was truncated, so the base rates and full span coverage of those samples are unknown.

view.series_note: traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans of every operation of the service (internal, client and server spans alike), summed over the labels kept in this query; it is not a count of requests. status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET means the span carried no status; it does not mean the call succeeded.
